notes: §1985:XIII.4.7.4 GR4: 'The TERMINATE statement cannot be executed for a report unless the TERMINATE statement was chronologically preceded by an INITIATE statement for that report and for which no TERMINATE statement has yet been executed'; no result is stated. TerminateCore does its work only for a report Initiate made active, and otherwise raises EC-REPORT-INACTIVE, which cannot be enabled at 85, and returns. Probes at 85: TERMINATE with no INITIATE, and a second TERMINATE, run with no output (one FINAL footing in the file) and no abend; INITIATE, GENERATE, TERMINATE, INITIATE, TERMINATE prints the witness's TERMINATE OK.

next.reason: Both require an initiated, not yet terminated report: 1985 'cannot be executed ... unless ... chronologically preceded by an INITIATE statement for that report and for which no TERMINATE statement has yet been executed'; 2023 'may be executed only for a report that is in the active state' (§2023:14.9.46.4 GR1), set by INITIATE (§2023:14.9.21.4 GR4) and ended by TERMINATE (§2023:14.9.46.4 GR2; §2023:13.8.4 prose defines the state). 1985 states no result for the violation, a run-time rule; 2023 defines one: 'the EC-REPORT-INACTIVE exception condition is set to exist and the execution of the statement has no other effect'. Different (now defined) result.
